quotes.text: After the Second War, he was present at the meeting with other kings of the Alliance in [Nethergarde Keep](/wiki/Nethergarde_Keep). Greymane complained about the expenses of the keep, though the newly crowned King of Stormwind [Varian Wrynn](/wiki/Varian_Wrynn) pointed out that a price couldn't be put on something as essential as their safety.[22]
After Archibald's death, Genn took the throne and led Gilneas much like his father had.

sources.title: Genn Greymane: Lord of His Pack - Media Gallery - World of Warcraft

quotes.text: “You want to wall off our entire nation? Close our borders and end trade with the rest of the Alliance? I… it is a rather large decision, would you not say?”

“Lord, as you’ve described, the other nations seem eager to assist. If Trollbane, Perenolde, and the rest partake, I do not know how we can rightfully call ourselves neighbors or friends if we do not join with them,” Crowley continued. Genn understood why he was so beloved. His words were spoken with acute vigor. There were no political angles at play -- just a man concerned for his fellow men. Genn respected him no matter how misguided he was. Crowley couldn’t possibly understand the folly of his sympathy, what it could actually lead to. He did not see that his own people, above all else, needed to be accounted for first. He was young and newer among the nobility.

“It is a path that does have merit, my lord,” Baron Ashbury added. Ashbury was one of Genn’s most trusted friends. Genn had grown up with him; his father, Lord Ashbury the 1st, had helped Archibald build the nation up, and Archibald had always told Genn to trust in the Ashburys’ fidelity to the crown.

“On this map it seems you are suggesting the possibility of Lord Marley’s realm…. But look at the terrain, my liege…. We have this mountainous region right here. What a grand hold that would make, with mountains on either side that would create a secure natural barrier.”
It was the smile that had made him fall in love with her all those years ago when they had first met at the Royal Aderic Banquet.

sources.title: Darius Crowley

quotes.text: At the time of the [Second War](/wiki/Second_War), Lord Crowley was a nobleman whose lands and people were in northern [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)), including some land outside of the border that would later be known as the [Greymane Wall](/wiki/Greymane_Wall). He owned the towns of [Pyrewood Village](/wiki/Pyrewood_Village) and [Ambermill](/wiki/Ambermill). Despite being young and new to the Gilnean council of Lords, his altruistic and charismatic qualities made him loved by the Gilnean people and earned him the respect and friendship of [King Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane). Crowley was one of the nobles who accompanied Greymane to [Capital City](/wiki/Capital_City) to hear of [Stormwind](/wiki/Stormwind_(kingdom))'s fall and [Anduin Lothar](/wiki/Anduin_Lothar) warning about the invading [Orcish Horde](/wiki/Orcish_Horde). Crowley was sympathetic to the Alliance's plight and advised Greymane to send aid to the newly-formed [Alliance](/wiki/Alliance_of_Lordaeron). Greymane agreed out of self-serving reasons but initially offered only token support.[1]

**Lord Darius Crowley** was once a [Gilnean](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)) nobleman. A pro-[Alliance](/wiki/Alliance_of_Lordaeron) figure, he dissented with King [Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane)'s decision to separate his people with the [Greymane Wall](/wiki/Greymane_Wall). Crowley led the [Northgate Rebellion](/wiki/Northgate_Rebellion) that caused a civil war in [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula), during which he was imprisoned. When Gilneas was attacked by [worgen](/wiki/Worgen), he was freed and became a worgen himself. Both Crowley and Greymane reconciled and joined forces against the threats Gilneas faced. He now leads the [Gilneas Liberation Front](/wiki/Gilneas_Liberation_Front) which fights against the Forsaken along with the [Bloodfang Pack](/wiki/Bloodfang_Pack) and the [7th Legion](/wiki/7th_Legion). When the [Burning Legion](/wiki/Burning_Legion) returned to assault Azeroth, Darius and his daughter [Lorna](/wiki/Lorna_Crowley) joined Genn on the *[Skyfire](/wiki/The_Skyfire)* as part of his army forces.

sources.title: Lord Vincent Godfrey

quotes.text: Following the end of the [Second War](/wiki/Second_War), Genn told Godfrey of his intentions of constructing the [Greymane Wall](/wiki/Greymane_Wall) to seal Gilneas off from the rest of the world. Godfrey pointed out that while Genn was considering building the wall through the lands of [Lord Marley](/wiki/Lord_Marley), constructing it through a mountainous region in Lord Crowley's domain would make for a more secure natural barrier, although doing so would cut off the northern villages of [Ambermill](/wiki/Ambermill) and [Pyrewood](/wiki/Pyrewood_Village). Genn warned that Darius might not take well to having his lands cut off, but Godfrey insisted that it was the best course of action for Gilneas. The fact that this placement of the wall would make Godfrey's own lands the most strategically valuable — as they would form the realm nearest to the wall and would thus be Gilneas' buffer to the outside — did not escape Genn, but he conceded that Godfrey was right, regardless of his personal motives. As Godfrey finished his goblet of wine, he fought the urge to smile.[4]

**Lord Vincent Godfrey**[3] is a renegade nobleman from [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula) who opposed his king, [Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane), after discovering that Genn and many of his people had been afflicted with the [worgen](/wiki/Worgen) curse. After committing suicide rather than acknowledge a worgen as his lord, Godfrey's body was recovered and reanimated by the [Forsaken](/wiki/Forsaken), but after turning on them as well, he fled into the abandoned ruins of [Shadowfang Keep](/wiki/Shadowfang_Keep), where he and his followers remain.

Prior to the [Second War](/wiki/Second_War), Godfrey was among the [Gilnean](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)) nobles who accompanied King [Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane) to [Lordaeron](/wiki/Lordaeron) to create the [Alliance of Lordaeron](/wiki/Alliance_of_Lordaeron).

sources.title: Baron Ashbury

quotes.text: He and [Genn](/wiki/Genn) grew up together, and he was once one of the king's most trusted friends. He was present in the [Capital City](/wiki/Capital_City) to create the [Alliance of Lordaeron](/wiki/Alliance_of_Lordaeron) and agreed with [Lord Godfrey](/wiki/Lord_Godfrey), to send only a token army. He participated in the hunts with Genn, [Lord Marley](/wiki/Lord_Marley) and Godfrey in the [Blackwald](/wiki/Blackwald).[1]

He joined with Lord [Vincent Godfrey](/wiki/Vincent_Godfrey) to turn [Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane) over to the [Forsaken](/wiki/Forsaken) in exchange for an end to hostilities. Along with his ally, [Lord Walden](/wiki/Lord_Walden), Ashbury was slain by Gilnean [worgen](/wiki/Worgen) who fought to save their King. Godfrey, Ashbury, and Walden were all raised in undeath by the Forsaken and served them for a time. After Godfrey betrayed the Forsaken by slaying [Sylvanas Windrunner](/wiki/Sylvanas_Windrunner), Ashbury fled with his master into nearby [Shadowfang Keep](/wiki/Shadowfang_Keep).

Instead he remained by Greymane's side until [Krennan Aranas](/wiki/Krennan_Aranas) sent an [adventurer](/wiki/Adventurer) to help.

sources.title: Shadowfang Keep

quotes.text: When the [Scourge](/wiki/Scourge) washed over Lordaeron, the Gilnean Archmage, [Arugal](/wiki/Arugal), investigated the research of the mage [Ur](/wiki/Ur). With the sorcerer's knowledge, Arugal summoned the [worgen](/wiki/Worgen) with the blessings of [Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane)[5] and against the advice of the [Kirin Tor](/wiki/Kirin_Tor).[6] The worgen successfully turned the tide against the Scourge, but became uncontrollable, attacking the [Gilnean military](/wiki/Gilnean_military). After this, Arugal's worgen ran rampant through Silverpine, eventually overwhelming the keep, killing Baron Silverlaine and his family. Distraught and broken, Arugal accepted the worgen as his [children](/wiki/Son_of_Arugal) and retreated into the keep and named the place Shadowfang Keep.[1] Communing with [Alpha Prime](/wiki/Alpha_Prime), he became a key servant of the [Wolf Cult](/wiki/Wolf_Cult), converting the humans of Silverpine into worgen, namely the [Moonrage](/wiki/Moonrage) and [Shadowfang packs](/wiki/Shadowfang_pack). Protected by his worgen minions as well as the ghosts of the fallen Baron and his household, Arugal served his master in converting most of the forest's remaining denizens to the curse, with locations such as [Deep Elem Mine](/wiki/Deep_Elem_Mine) falling as well as Pyrewood.[7]

quotes.text: **Isiden Perenolde**[1] was the nephew of Lord [Aiden Perenolde](/wiki/Aiden_Perenolde), King of [Alterac](/wiki/Alterac_(kingdom)). When Alterac was placed under martial law by order of King [Terenas](/wiki/Terenas_Menethil_II), Isiden fled to [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula), where he hoped to rally support.[2] He was eventually backed by [Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane), [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom))' king, as the matter of the succession began to heat up.[3]
Nothing has been heard from Isiden since then and his status is unknown.

sources.title: Innkeeper

quotes.text: Frustrated by the [Dalaran wizards](/wiki/Kirin_Tor)' lack of progress against the [undead](/wiki/Undead) during the [Third War](/wiki/Third_War), the [Archmage Arugal](/wiki/Arugal) elected to summon the extra-dimensional [worgen](/wiki/Worgen) to bolster his side's diminishing ranks. The wolf-men slaughtered the [Scourge](/wiki/Scourge), then quickly turned on the wizards themselves and laid siege to the keep of the noble, [Baron Silverlaine](/wiki/Baron_Silverlaine). The fort quickly fell into shadow and ruin. Driven mad with guilt, Arugal adopted the worgen as his children and retreated to the newly dubbed 'Shadowfang Keep'.

sources.title: Know Your Lore: Shadowfang Keep

quotes.text: Yes, before it was a dungeon, Shadowfang Keep was the ancestral home of [Baron Silverlaine](http://www.wowhead.com/npc=3887) , a noble who owed allegiance to Gilneas and whose ancestral lands lay just outside of where the Greymane Wall would be erected. Ruling over the settlers of neaby Pyrewood Village, the Baron seemed a relatively capable leader... until, of course, the coming of the Scourge.
